title: The Swing
description: Keep a griever swinging between grief and daily life through the first year after a loss.

title: Ageism Quiz
description: Ten questions on how ageism shapes grief and end-of-life care. Show your score screen to the class.

title: Line Charades
description: Two teams take turns acting out a secret line of Emily Dickinson's “Because I could not stop for Death —” while their guesser finds it in the poem.
concept: Close reading of poetry about death

title: Term Duel
description: Rock-paper-scissors your way around the room: win and name a term, lose and explain it. Tick off every term on your own phone. Pick a topic each week.
concept: Course vocabulary: Advance Care Planning; Models of Grief

title: Technique Draw
description: Read a bilingual couples case, then draw a random grief-therapy technique as many times as you like and decide how you would adapt it.
players: Whole class, one phone each (or projector)
concept: Dual Process Model with grieving couples (Hooghe, 2022); grief techniques (Neimeyer, 2016)

title: In Their Footsteps
description: The mourner wanders a beach, forest, meadow and snowfield; the path glows, then fades. The companion retraces it from memory: same route, same order, same pace. Unlocks with a code shown in class.
concept: Companioning the bereaved: walking alongside, learning from others (Wolfelt, 2009)

title: Palliative Shift
description: You’re the social worker on a palliative care ward: flag what each patient needs, watch which medicine drawers the nurse opens, and answer families’ worries accurately without overstepping your role. Chinese and English throughout. Unlocks with a code shown in class.
concept: Palliative care knowledge for social workers, based on the Palliative Care Knowledge Test (Nakazawa et al., 2009)

title: Bereavement Shift
description: Run a bereavement clinic for a week: screen grieving people and walk each one to the care that fits. Hold a case conference before PGD therapy, lead families together, and keep the clinic from being overloaded. Top-5 team scores. Unlocks with a code shown in class.
players: 1–2 players on the projector (8BitDo or keyboard), or 1 on a tablet
concept: Resilience, prolonged grief disorder (DSM-5-TR, PG-13-R; Prigerson et al., 2021) and matching care to need

title: Light in the Stacks
description: Doze off in a lecture and wake up three years ago in the campus library. Relearn prolonged grief disorder with the school counselor (in Chinese, quizzed on the English terms), then search three dark basement floors, past eight shadows named for the Criterion C symptoms, to find a grieving friend before your phone dies. Unlocks with a code shown in class.
players: 1 player on a phone or tablet, or 2 on the projector (one drives, one reads)
concept: Prolonged grief disorder (DSM-5-TR criteria, PG-13-R), screening, asking about suicide and referral; bereavement care tiers
